acceptance_criteria: Net daily edge after the SPY round-trip spread cost is positive
spec.alternative_hypothesis: The lagged BAA10Y change (basis points, latest available at the decision close) has a negative coefficient in the daily BAA10Y->SPX partial lead-lag regression (spread widening predicts weaker next-day SPX returns), with partial R-squared at least 0.005 and a positive holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared. Note on wording: the planner draft's 'positive, out-of-sample component' refers to positive incremental explanatory power (incremental R-squared above zero), not to a positive coefficient — the expected coefficient sign is negative.
spec.benchmark: Own-history baseline: next-day SPX return predicted from its own lagged return and the lagged VIX common-factor control only, without the lagged BAA10Y change
cost_assumptions: SPY is the tradable S&P 500 instrument; $0 commission at major brokers (assumed, not verified for the user's account)
Bid-ask spread 1bp per side, deliberately conservative against realised SPY spreads of about 0.1-0.2bp
Slippage and market impact ignored; both would reduce any edge
The sign rule trades at the close; no intraday execution is modelled
spec.cost_model: SPY ETF as the tradable instrument: $0 commission; bid-ask spread assumed 1bp per side (conservative — realised SPY spreads are about 0.1-0.2bp), so a round trip costs 2bp per position flip and 1bp for entry from flat or final exit; sign rule on holdout out-of-sample augmented forecasts, 1x, always invested while positioned. Slippage and market impact ignored; both would reduce any edge. No funding cost (unlevered ETF).
exclusions: Bars outside the sample window (2003-01-02 to 2026-11-18) are out of sample.
Incomplete synchronized rows are excluded and counted.
FRED empty-field missing values and Yahoo null closes are excluded at fetch time and counted.
The first two panel return rows have no lagged BAA10Y change and are dropped.
The naive unlagged alignment, the no-factor control, the reverse placebo and the sub-period stability split are descriptive only and are not in the test family.
known_confounders: BAA10Y is defined as the BAA yield minus the 10-year Treasury yield (DGS10); the spread change nets out the rates level by construction, so a common rates shock moves both legs and is differenced out — the predictor measures the credit-specific component. The DGS10 leg is therefore not a separate control.

The 2-trading-day BAA10Y availability lag is verified behaviorally (6b evidence probe 2026-11-18T21:45Z plus the fetch-time re-check) and assumed constant across the sample. If the historical posting lag differed, the predictor alignment is wrong for those periods.
FRED series are revised over time; the fetch records the current vintage. Historical values as first published may differ from the current vintage (revision risk is unmodelled).

The VIX control is itself a FRED series with the standard 1-trading-day publication lag; the control uses the latest available VIX change (lagged 1 step), not the same-day change, so it cannot absorb the day-t common shock in full.
The sample covers the 2008 crisis, the 2020 COVID crash and the 2022 hiking cycle; transmission may be regime-dependent. Sub-period stability is descriptive only.
SPX log returns are close-to-close; the sign-rule cost gate assumes trading at the close with no slippage.

The PIT store records available_at equal to the event time (adapter limitation); the publication lag is enforced in the trial's panel construction via the study-007 lagged-changes module, not in the stored observations.
spec.mechanism: A widening BAA credit spread reflects rising credit risk premia and tightening financial conditions: corporate funding costs rise relative to Treasuries as default risk is repriced. Equity markets follow with a lag as the higher cost of capital and weaker risk appetite feed into equity valuations. The spread is an end-of-day published signal, so any transmission should appear the next trading day. The expected sign is negative: spread widening predicts weaker next-day SPX returns.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count. FRED empty-field missing values and Yahoo null closes are excluded at fetch time and counted.
model_definition: Partial lead-lag OLS with Newey-West HAC standard errors (daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day SPX return)
Purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation of the primary model (baseline: own history plus lagged VIX control; augmented: plus lagged BAA10Y change)
Naive lead-lag scan (lags 0-5, raw Pearson correlations) as a descriptive upper bound (not in the test family)
Descriptive only: unlagged (naive) alignment, no-factor upper-bound control, reverse placebo (SPX->BAA10Y), sub-period stability
spec.multiple_testing_family: Credit-spread transmission to the S&P 500 (1 test: daily lagged BAA10Y change -> next-day SPX return)
spec.null_hypothesis: Lagged BAA10Y changes have no incremental predictive value for next-day SPX returns over the S&P 500's own history and the lagged VIX common-factor control, after costs and dependence controls.
spec.primary_metric: Partial R-squared of the lagged BAA10Y change (bp, latest available at the decision close) in the daily BAA10Y->SPX partial lead-lag regression
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted primary p-value at or above 0.05
Holdout out-of-sample incremental R-squared at or below 0
Net daily edge after costs is zero or negative
spec.research_question: Does the most recent BAA10Y credit-spread change available at the close predict the next-day S&P 500 log return beyond the S&P 500's own history and the lagged VIX common-factor control?
spec.target_definition: Next-day close-to-close SPX log return (Yahoo ^GSPC); the predictor is the most recent BAA10Y level change in basis points available at the decision close — under the verified 2-trading-day BAA10Y posting lag, the change ending two trading days before the decision close.
spec.title: Credit-spread changes lead S&P 500 returns
